title: Power Pages: OpenID Connect sign-in accepts encrypted ID tokens
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap targets and automatic enablement, and distinguishes existing authentication controls from undocumented encrypted-token configuration. Minor improvements are to acknowledge an alternative navigation path in Microsoft's release plan and explicitly list the claims-mapping controls recommended in the checklist.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans for Power Pages OpenID Connect authentication to accept encrypted ID tokens in addition to signed tokens.
claims.quote: This feature adds support for token-level encryption during authentication, allowing Power Pages to accept encrypted ID tokens in addition to signed tokens.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: OpenID Connect governance is reached in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > OpenID Connect > environment > Manage.
claims.quote:
Under Products, select Power Pages.
Select the Settings tab.
Under Authentication, select the authentication option you want to manage.
Select an environment, and then select Manage.
claims.fix: Keep the cited operational path. Note that https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/release-plan/2025wave2/power-pages/manage-external-authentication-provider-governance instead gives Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers. Also mention that after Manage the administrator chooses all, specific, excluded or no sites before reviewing and applying the change.
